review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Dry Tortugas telemetry supports seasonal spawning migrations and reef-site fidelity; numeric depth and SST suitability bands remain provisional.

To use a real photo: replace that file with a transparent PNG of the same name (cropped tight to the fish, facing left looks best), then set kind to "photo" and fill in credit and license here. profile.size: FWC reports up to about 30 inches and 25 lb; Florida state record 30 lb 4 oz.
profile.diet: Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and snails.
profile.depth: Coastal waters near structure. Adults commonly use reefs, ledges and shelf-edge habitat; juveniles use shallower vegetated nursery habitats. The existing 25-95 m depth range is not a universal species depth preference and is retained only as a provisional model screening range.
profile.behavior: Adults associate with reefs, ledges, wrecks and other structure; juveniles use shallow seagrass and mangrove habitat. In the Florida Keys, adults make seasonal movements to known spawning aggregation sites, including Riley's Hump in the Dry Tortugas. Aggregation locations are discrete and should not be inferred from generic reef polygons.
profile.spawning: FWC's Florida species profile reports spawning in July and August. Florida Keys research documents seasonal spawning migrations and aggregations at discrete sites. Full-moon timing and aggregation behavior are location-specific and should not be treated as a universal calendar for all reefs.
profile.regulations_note: Florida minimum size is 18 inches total length; daily limit is 5 per person within the 10-fish snapper aggregate. Open year-round, subject to area-specific closures such as Western Dry Rocks.

factors.value_notes: Florida reef habitat and Dry Tortugas telemetry support adult association with reef home sites and discrete spawning grounds. Juveniles use shallow vegetated nursery habitat. The study does not validate the exact score ranking among runtime structure categories, and generic reef polygons must not be treated as known spawning aggregation sites.

Adult reef association and documented movements between resident reef habitat and Riley's Hump support the broader relevance of reef edges and discrete reef features. The cited angler source does not establish a quantitative preference for the runtime bottom_curvature metric or its monotonic score.
factors.reason_template: Sharp bottom curvature indicates a terrace edge or reef break line.

factors.value_notes: Available sources describe adult reef habitat, shallow juvenile nursery areas and spawning-site movements, but do not validate the configured 15-120 m range or 25-70 m ideal as a species-specific depth preference. Life stage and local reef context matter; numeric values remain unchanged and provisional.
factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in the reef water adult mutton snapper use.

factors.value_notes: Dry Tortugas telemetry found spawning migrations during a seasonal warming period of roughly 25-30 °C, while separate adult acoustic telemetry found no evidence of selection for specific available temperatures. Seasonal exposure is not a thermal preference curve and does not validate the configured 19-31 °C range or 22-29.5 °C ideal.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, within the currently configured provisional screening band for mutton snapper; this is not a validated thermal tolerance.

factors.value_notes: Acoustic telemetry of 55 mutton snapper in the Dry Tortugas (2008-2012) documented spawning migrations from April through August, linked to lunar timing and seasonal warming. This supports a local Florida Keys/Tortugas spawning period, but the configured May-August window omits observed April movements and the June-July peak scores are not independently validated as catch peaks.

value_text.peak: It is peak mutton snapper season (about June and July), when fish gather to spawn.
value_text.in_season: It is mutton snapper spawning-aggregation season (about May to August).
value_text.off: It is outside the main spawning season, though mutton snapper are caught year-round.

timing.note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs. Reports disagree on mutton snapper: some captains say day trips, others night.

text.dusk: It is dusk, when snappers are reported to bite better and keep biting into the night.
text.night: It is night, when charter captains report their best snapper action.

moon.text: It is the week around the full moon in spawning season, when mutton snapper gather on reef edges to spawn.

regulations.summary: Florida Atlantic and Gulf waters: 18 inches total length minimum; 5 per person per day within the 10-fish snapper aggregate; open year-round. Area-specific closures apply, including Western Dry Rocks April 1-July 31.
regulations.bag_limit: 5 per person per day within the 10-fish snapper aggregate
regulations.season: Open year-round, subject to area-specific closures and protected-area rules
regulations.jurisdiction: Florida Atlantic and Gulf state/federal waters; special Biscayne National Park and Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary area rules may apply
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: FWC currently lists 18-inch total length and 5 per person within the 10-snapper aggregate. Western Dry Rocks seasonal closure is April 1-July 31. Verify sanctuary and park closures for exact coordinates; do not assume all offshore reef areas are open.

open_items: The existing numeric SST and broad depth scoring bands remain provisional and unchanged pending primary physiological/depth-preference evidence.
Known spawning aggregation sites and their seasonal protections are spatially specific; do not infer aggregation habitat from generic reef layers alone.
